Reports pointless bitwise expressions.

Such expressions include applying the & operator to the maximum value for the given type, applying the or operator to zero, and shifting by zero. Such expressions may be the result of automated refactorings not followed through to completion and are unlikely to be originally intended.

Examples:


  // Warning: operation is pointless and can be replaced with just `flags`
  // 0xFFFF_FFFF is the maximum value for an integer, and both literals are treated
  // as 32 bit integer literals.
  int bits = flags & 0xFFFF_FFFF;

  // Warning: operation is pointless and can be replaced with just `bits`
  // OR-ing with 0 always outputs the other operand.
  int or = bits | 0x0;

  // Warning: operation is pointless, as always results in 0
  int xor = or ^ or;
target:
Meldet sinnlose Bitweise-Ausdrücke.

Dazu gehört das Anwenden des &-Operators auf den Maximalwert eines Typs, das Anwenden des or-Operators auf null und das Verschieben um null. Solche Ausdrücke können das Ergebnis nicht vollständig durchgeführter automatisierter Refaktorierungen sein und sind selten so beabsichtigt.

Beispiele:


  // Warnung: Operation ist sinnlos und kann durch `flags` ersetzt werden
  // 0xFFFF_FFFF ist der Maximalwert für einen Integer, und beide Literale werden
  // als 32-Bit-Integer-Literale behandelt.
  int bits = flags & 0xFFFF_FFFF;

  // Warnung: Operation ist sinnlos und kann durch `bits` ersetzt werden
  // OR mit 0 ergibt immer den anderen Operanden.
  int or = bits | 0x0;

  // Warnung: Operation ist sinnlos, da das Ergebnis immer 0 ist
  int xor = or ^ or;

source:
Reports classes that may be serialized or deserialized.

A class may be serialized if it supports the Serializable interface, and its readObject() and writeObject() methods are not defined to always throw an exception. Serializable classes may be dangerous in code intended for secure use.

Example:


  class DeserializableClass implements Serializable { // the class doesn't contain 'writeObject()' method throwing an exception
    private int sensitive = 736326;

    private void readObject(ObjectInputStream in) {
        throw new Error();
    }
}

After the quick-fix is applied:


  class DeserializableClass implements Serializable {
    private int sensitive = 736326;

    private void readObject(ObjectInputStream in) {
        throw new Error();
    }

    private void writeObject(java.io.ObjectOutputStream out) throws java.io.IOException {
        throw new java.io.NotSerializableException("DeserializableClass");
    }
  }

Use the following options to configure the inspection:

  • List classes whose inheritors should not be reported by this inspection. This is meant for classes that inherit Serializable from a superclass but are not intended for serialization. Note that it still may be more secure to add readObject() and writeObject() methods which always throw an exception, instead of ignoring those classes.
  • Whether to ignore serializable anonymous classes.
target:
Meldet Klassen, die serialisiert oder deserialisiert werden können.

Eine Klasse kann serialisiert werden, wenn sie die Serializable-Schnittstelle unterstützt, und ihre readObject()- und writeObject()-Methoden nicht so definiert sind, dass sie immer eine Exception werfen. Serialisierbare Klassen können in Code, der für sichere Verwendung gedacht ist, gefährlich sein.

Beispiel:


  class DeserializableClass implements Serializable { // die Klasse enthält keine 'writeObject()'-Methode, die eine Exception wirft
    private int sensitive = 736326;

    private void readObject(ObjectInputStream in) {
        throw new Error();
    }
}

Nach Anwendung des Quick-Fix:


  class DeserializableClass implements Serializable {
    private int sensitive = 736326;

    private void readObject(ObjectInputStream in) {
        throw new Error();
    }

    private void writeObject(java.io.ObjectOutputStream out) throws java.io.IOException {
        throw new java.io.NotSerializableException("DeserializableClass");
    }
  }

Verwenden Sie die folgenden Optionen, um die Inspection zu konfigurieren:

  • Listen Sie Klassen auf, deren Erben von dieser Inspection nicht gemeldet werden sollen. Dies ist für Klassen gedacht, die Serializable von einer Superklasse erben, aber nicht für die Serialisierung vorgesehen sind. Beachten Sie, dass es dennoch sicherer sein kann, readObject()- und writeObject()-Methoden hinzuzufügen, die immer eine Exception werfen, anstatt diese Klassen zu ignorieren.
  • Ob serialisierbare anonyme Klassen ignoriert werden sollen.

source:
Applies to new Spring Configuration that are created by invoking New | Spring Component | Configuration in the Project tool window.
This built-in template is editable. Along with Kotlin expressions and comments, you can also use the predefined variables (listed below) that will then be expanded like macros into corresponding values.

It is also possible to specify custom variables. Custom variables use the following format: ${VARIABLE_NAME}, where VARIABLE_NAME is a name for your variable (for example, ${MY_CUSTOM_FUNCTION_NAME}). Before the IDE creates a new file with custom variables, you see a dialog where you can define values for custom variables in the template.

By using the #parse directive, you can include templates from the Includes tab. To include a template, specify the full name of the template as a parameter in quotation marks (for example, #parse("File Header.java").
Predefined variables take the following values:
${PACKAGE_NAME}   Name of the package in which a new class is created
${NAME}   Name of the new class specified by you in the Create New Class dialog
${USER}   System login name of the current user
${DATE}   Current system date
${TIME}   Current system time
${YEAR}   Current year
${MONTH}   Current month
${MONTH_NAME_SHORT}   First 3 letters of the current month name (Jan, Feb, and so on)
${MONTH_NAME_FULL}   Full name of the current month (January, February, and so on)
${DAY}   Current day of the month
${HOUR}   Current hour
${MINUTE}   Current minute
${PROJECT_NAME}   Name of the current project
target:

Es ist auch möglich, benutzerdefinierte Variablen anzugeben. Benutzerdefinierte Variablen verwenden das folgende Format: ${VARIABLE_NAME}, wobei VARIABLE_NAME ein Name für Ihre Variable ist (zum Beispiel ${MY_CUSTOM_FUNCTION_NAME}). Bevor die IDE eine neue Datei mit benutzerdefinierten Variablen erstellt, wird ein Dialog angezeigt, in dem Sie Werte für benutzerdefinierte Variablen in der Vorlage definieren können.

Mit der #parse-Direktive können Sie Vorlagen aus der Registerkarte Includes einbinden. Um eine Vorlage einzubinden, geben Sie den vollständigen Namen der Vorlage als Parameter in Anführungszeichen an (zum Beispiel #parse("File Header.java").
Vordefinierte Variablen nehmen die folgenden Werte an:

Applies to new Spring Configuration that are created by invoking New | Spring Component | Configuration in the Project tool window.
This built-in template is editable. Along with Java expressions and comments, you can also use the predefined variables (listed below) that will then be expanded like macros into corresponding values.

It is also possible to specify custom variables. Custom variables use the following format: ${VARIABLE_NAME}, where VARIABLE_NAME is a name for your variable (for example, ${MY_CUSTOM_FUNCTION_NAME}). Before the IDE creates a new file with custom variables, you see a dialog where you can define values for custom variables in the template.

By using the #parse directive, you can include templates from the Includes tab. To include a template, specify the full name of the template as a parameter in quotation marks (for example, #parse("File Header.java").
Predefined variables take the following values:
${PACKAGE_NAME}   Name of the package in which a new class is created
${NAME}   Name of the new class specified by you in the Create New Class dialog
${USER}   System login name of the current user
${DATE}   Current system date
${TIME}   Current system time
${YEAR}   Current year
${MONTH}   Current month
${MONTH_NAME_SHORT}   First 3 letters of the current month name (Jan, Feb, and so on)
${MONTH_NAME_FULL}   Full name of the current month (January, February, and so on)
${DAY}   Current day of the month
${HOUR}   Current hour
${MINUTE}   Current minute
${PROJECT_NAME}   Name of the current project

Reports coroutine builders calls that violate structured concurrency by accepting a CoroutineContext containing a Job.

Passing contexts with a Job to coroutine builders like launch, async, produce, promise, or to withContext breaks the parent-child relationship between coroutines, defeating the purpose of structured concurrency.

Example:


coroutineScope.launch(Job()) {
  // this coroutine does not have parent relationship with the `coroutineScope` receiver 
}
target:
Meldet Aufrufe von Coroutinen-Buildern, die die strukturierte Nebenläufigkeit verletzen, indem sie einen CoroutineContext mit einem Job akzeptieren.

Die Übergabe von Kontexten mit einem Job an Coroutinen-Builder wie launch, async, produce, promise oder an withContext unterbricht die Eltern-Kind-Beziehung zwischen Coroutinen und untergräbt den Zweck der strukturierten Nebenläufigkeit.

Beispiel:


coroutineScope.launch(Job()) {
  // this coroutine does not have parent relationship with the `coroutineScope` receiver 
}

Reports return of, or assignment from a method parameter to a field of an array or a mutable type such as Collection, Date, Map, Calendar, etc.

Because such types are mutable, this construct may result in unexpected modifications of an object's state from outside the owning class. Although this construct may be useful for performance reasons, it is inherently prone to bugs.

The following mutable types are reported:

  • java.util.Date
  • java.util.Calendar
  • java.util.Collection
  • java.util.Map
  • com.google.common.collect.Multimap
  • com.google.common.collect.Table

The quick-fix adds a call to the field's .clone() method for arrays or uses an unmodifiable collection wrapper.

Example:


  import java.util.*;
  class Log {
    private String[] messages = {"one", "two", "three"};
    private Map<String, String> map = new HashMap<>();

    String[] getMessages() {
      return messages; // warning: Return of String[] field 'messages'
    }

    Map<String, String> mapping() {
      return map; // warning: Return of Map<String, String> field 'map'
    }
  }

After the quick-fix is applied:


  import java.util.*;
  class Log {
    String[] messages = {"one", "two", "three"};
    private Map<String, String> map = new HashMap<>();

    String[] getMessages() {
      return messages.clone();
    }

    Map<String, String> mapping() {
      return Collections.unmodifiableMap(map);
    }
  }

Use the Ignore assignments in and returns from private methods option to ignore assignments and returns in private methods.
target:
Meldet die Rückgabe oder Zuweisung eines Methodenparameters an ein Feld eines Arrays oder eines veränderlichen Typs wie Collection, Date, Map, Calendar usw.

Da solche Typen veränderlich sind, kann dieses Konstrukt zu unerwarteten Änderungen des Objektzustands von außerhalb der besitzenden Klasse führen. Obwohl dieses Konstrukt aus Performancegründen nützlich sein kann, ist es von Natur aus fehleranfällig.

Die folgenden veränderlichen Typen werden gemeldet:

  • java.util.Date
  • java.util.Calendar
  • java.util.Collection
  • java.util.Map
  • com.google.common.collect.Multimap
  • com.google.common.collect.Table

Der Quick-Fix fügt für Arrays einen Aufruf der .clone()-Methode des Feldes hinzu oder verwendet einen unveränderlichen Collection-Wrapper.

Beispiel:


  import java.util.*;
  class Log {
    private String[] messages = {"one", "two", "three"};
    private Map<String, String> map = new HashMap<>();

    String[] getMessages() {
      return messages; // warning: Return of String[] field 'messages'
    }

    Map<String, String> mapping() {
      return map; // warning: Return of Map<String, String> field 'map'
    }
  }

Reports a declarations that are propagated by @Deprecated annotation that will lead to compilation error since 1.9.

Motivation types:

  • Implementation changes are required for implementation design/architectural reasons
  • Inconsistency in the design (things are done differently in different contexts)

More details: KT-47902: Do not propagate method deprecation through overrides

The quick-fix copies @Deprecated annotation from the parent declaration.

Example:


  open class Base {
      @Deprecated("Don't use")
      open fun foo() {}
  }

  class Derived : Base() {
      override fun foo() {}
  }

After the quick-fix is applied:


  open class Base {
      @Deprecated("Don't use")
      open fun foo() {}
  }

  class Derived : Base() {
      @Deprecated("Don't use")
      override fun foo() {}
  }

This inspection only reports if the Kotlin language level of the project or module is 1.6 or higher.

source:
Reports methods that override a super method without calling it. This is also known as a refused bequest. Such methods may represent a failure of abstraction and cause hard-to-trace bugs.

The inspection doesn't report methods overridden from java.lang.Object, except for clone(). The clone() method should by convention call its super method, which will return an object of the correct type.

Example 1:


  class A {
    @Override
    public Object clone() {
      // does not call 'super.clone()'
      return new A();
    }
  }

Example 2:


  interface I {
    default void foo() {}
  }

  class A implements I {
    // warning on method when
    // 'Ignore 'default' super methods' is disabled
    @Override
    public void foo(){}
  }

Configure the inspection:

  • Use the Only report when super method is annotated by option to ignore super methods marked with the annotations from the provided list. You can manually add annotations to the list.
  • Use the Ignore empty super methods option to ignore super methods that are either empty or only throw an exception.
  • Use the Ignore 'default' super methods option to ignore default super methods from interfaces.
target:

Beispiel 1:


  class A {

    // Warnung bei Methode, wenn

source:
Reports method parameters named identically to a field of a surrounding class. As a result of such naming, you may accidentally use the parameter when using the identically named field is intended.

A quick-fix is suggested to rename the parameter.

Example:


  class Main {
    private String value;

    public Main(String value) {
      value = value.toUpperCase();
    }
  }

You can configure the following options for this inspection:

  1. Ignore for property setters - ignore parameters of simple setters.
  2. Ignore superclass fields not visible from subclass - ignore private fields in a superclass, which are not visible from the method.
  3. Ignore for constructors - ignore parameters of constructors.
  4. Ignore for abstract methods - ignore parameters of abstract methods.
  5. Ignore for static method parameters hiding instance fields - ignore parameters of static methods hiding an instance field and to ignore parameters of instance methods in static inner classes hiding an instance field of an outer class. While not strictly hiding, such parameters can still be confusing.

source:
Reports usages of deprecated classes, fields, and methods. A quick-fix is available to automatically convert the deprecated usage, when the necessary information can be extracted from the Javadoc of the deprecated member.

Example:


  class Interesting {

    /**
     * @deprecated Use {@link #newHotness()} instead
     */
    @Deprecated
    public void oldAndBusted() {}

    public void newHotness() {}
  }
  class ElseWhere {
    void x(Interesting i) {
      i.oldAndBusted(); // deprecated warning here
    }
  }

After the quick-fix is applied:


  class Interesting {

    /**
     * @deprecated Use {@link #newHotness()} instead
     */
    @Deprecated
    public void oldAndBusted() {}

    public void newHotness() {}
  }
  class ElseWhere {
    void x(Interesting i) {
      i.newHotness();
    }
  }

By default, the inspection doesn't produce a warning if it's impossible or hard to avoid it. For example, the following code won't be reported:


  abstract class A { //library code
     @Deprecated
     abstract void m();
  }
  class B extends A { //project code
     @Override
     void m() {
        //doSmth;
     }
  }

Configure the inspection:

Use the options to disable this inspection inside deprecated members, overrides of abstract deprecated methods, non-static import statements, methods of deprecated classes, or same top-level classes.
target:
Meldet Verwendungen veralteter Klassen, Felder und Methoden. Es steht ein Quick-Fix zur Verfügung, um die veraltete Verwendung automatisch zu konvertieren, sofern die erforderlichen Informationen aus dem Javadoc des veralteten Mitglieds extrahiert werden können.

Beispiel:


  class Interesting {

    /**
     * @deprecated Use {@link #newHotness()} instead
     */
    @Deprecated
    public void oldAndBusted() {}

    public void newHotness() {}
  }
  class ElseWhere {
    void x(Interesting i) {
      i.oldAndBusted(); // deprecated warning here
    }
  }

Nach Anwendung des Quick-Fix:


  class Interesting {

    /**
     * @deprecated Use {@link #newHotness()} instead
     */
    @Deprecated
    public void oldAndBusted() {}

    public void newHotness() {}
  }
  class ElseWhere {
    void x(Interesting i) {
      i.newHotness();
    }
  }

Standardmäßig erzeugt die Inspektion keine Warnung, wenn sie nicht oder nur schwer vermeidbar ist. Zum Beispiel wird der folgende Code nicht gemeldet:


  abstract class A { //library code
     @Deprecated
     abstract void m();
  }
  class B extends A { //project code
     @Override
     void m() {
        //doSmth;
     }
  }

Inspektion konfigurieren:

Example:

    public String getName() {
      return name;

    @Override
    public String toString() {
      return getName();
    }
  }

After the quick-fix is applied:


  public class Salient {
    private String name;

    public String getName() {
      return name;
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
      return name;
    }
  }

Use the following options to configure the inspection:

  • Whether to only report getter calls on this, not on objects of the same type passed in as a parameter.

Reports calls from Kotlin to values() method in enum classes that can be replaced with entries property read.

Use of Enum.entries may improve performance of your code.

The quick-fix replaces values() with entries.

More details: KT-48872 Provide modern and performant replacement for Enum.values()

Note: entries property type is different from the return type of values() method (EnumEntries<T> which inherits from List<T> instead of Array<T>). Due to this in some cases quick fix inserts extra .toTypedArray() conversion to not break the code, but for most common cases replacement will be done without it (e.g. in for loop).

Example:


    enum class Version {
        V1, V2
    }

    Version.values().forEach { /* .. */ }
    val firstVersion = Version.values()[0]
    functionExpectingArray(Version.values())

After the quick-fix is applied:


    enum class Version {
        V1, V2
    }

    Version.entries.forEach { /* .. */ }
    val firstVersion = Version.entries[0]
    functionExpectingArray(Version.entries.toTypedArray())
target:

Der Quick-Fix ersetzt values() durch entries.

Weitere Details: KT-48872 Provide modern and performant replacement for Enum.values()

Hinweis: Der Typ der entries-Eigenschaft unterscheidet sich vom Rückgabetyp der values()-Methode (EnumEntries<T>, die von List<T> erbt, statt Array<T>). Deshalb fügt der Quick-Fix in manchen Fällen eine zusätzliche .toTypedArray()-Konvertierung ein, um den Code nicht zu brechen; in den meisten Fällen (z. B. in einer for-Schleife) erfolgt die Ersetzung jedoch ohne diese Konvertierung.

Beispiel:


    enum class Version {
        V1, V2
    }

    Version.values().forEach { /* .. */ }
    val firstVersion = Version.values()[0]
    functionExpectingArray(Version.values())

Nach Anwendung des Quick-Fix:


    enum class Version {
        V1, V2
    }

    Version.entries.forEach { /* .. */ }
    val firstVersion = Version.entries[0]
    functionExpectingArray(Version.entries.toTypedArray())

Reports construction of sorted collections, for example TreeSet, that rely on natural ordering, whose element type doesn't implement the Comparable interface.

It's unlikely that such a collection will work properly.

A false positive is possible if the collection element type is a non-comparable super-type, but the collection is intended to only hold comparable sub-types. Even if this is the case, it's better to narrow the collection element type or declare the super-type as Comparable because the mentioned approach is error-prone.

The inspection also reports cases when the collection element is a type parameter which is not declared as extends Comparable. You can suppress the warnings on type parameters using the provided option (for example, to keep the API compatibility).

New in 2018.3
target:

Ein Fehlalarm ist möglich, wenn der Element-Typ ein nicht vergleichbarer Super-Typ ist, die Collection aber nur vergleichbare Sub-Typen aufnehmen soll. Auch in diesem Fall ist es besser, den Element-Typ enger zu fassen oder den Super-Typ als Comparable zu deklarieren, weil der genannte Ansatz fehleranfällig ist.

Die Inspection meldet ebenfalls Fälle, in denen das Element ein Typ-Parameter ist, der nicht als extends Comparable deklariert ist. Über die Option lassen sich Warnungen zu Typ-Parametern unterdrücken (z. B. um die API-Kompatibilität zu wahren).

source:
Reports redundant asSequence() call that can never have a positive performance effect.

asSequence() speeds up collection processing that includes multiple operations because it performs operations lazily and doesn't create intermediate collections.

However, if a terminal operation (such as toList()) is used right after asSequence(), this doesn't give you any positive performance effect.

Example:


  fun test(list: List<String>) {
      list.asSequence().last()
  }

After the quick-fix is applied:


  fun test(list: List<String>) {
      list.last()
  }
target:
Meldet redundante asSequence()-Aufrufe, die niemals einen positiven Performance-Effekt haben können.

asSequence() beschleunigt die Verarbeitung von Collections mit mehreren Operationen, da Operationen verzögert ausgeführt werden und keine Zwischen-Collections erstellt werden.

Wird jedoch eine terminale Operation (wie toList()) direkt nach asSequence() verwendet, ergibt sich kein positiver Performance-Effekt.

Beispiel:


  fun test(list: List<String>) {
      list.asSequence().last()
  }

Nach Anwendung des Quick-Fix:


  fun test(list: List<String>) {
      list.last()
  }

Reports value parameter annotation usages without an explicit target for which the default target might be unexpected and undesirable.

The value parameter annotations without an explicit target are applied only to the parameter itself until Kotlin 2.1.20. For annotations applicable to both parameters and fields or properties, this behavior might be unintended when the annotation is used on a val or var constructor parameter.

Example: 


class Example(
    @Param val foo: String,
    @ParamField val bar: String, // the field is not annotated, only the parameter is
    @ParamProperty val baz: String, // the property is not annotated, only the parameter is
    @ParamProperty boo: String,
)

@Target(AnnotationTarget.VALUE_PARAMETER)
annotation class Param
@Target(AnnotationTarget.VALUE_PARAMETER, AnnotationTarget.FIELD)
annotation class ParamField
@Target(AnnotationTarget.VALUE_PARAMETER, AnnotationTarget.PROPERTY)
annotation class ParamProperty

After the quick-fix is applied:


class Example(
    @Param val foo: String,
    @field:ParamField val bar: String,
    @property:ParamProperty val baz: String,
    @ParamProperty boo: String,
)

@Target(AnnotationTarget.VALUE_PARAMETER)
annotation class Param
@Target(AnnotationTarget.VALUE_PARAMETER, AnnotationTarget.FIELD)
annotation class ParamField
@Target(AnnotationTarget.VALUE_PARAMETER, AnnotationTarget.PROPERTY)
annotation class ParamProperty

Reports request matchers in an authorizeHttpRequests / authorizeRequests chain that are unreachable because an earlier, more general matcher already covers them.

Spring Security evaluates matchers in declaration order and the first matching rule wins, so a specific rule placed after a more general one that also matches it is silently ignored. More specific matchers must come first.

Incorrect (the marked rules are ignored):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/home").hasRole("USER")        // covered by the earlier "/home"
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/**").hasRole("USER")
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/test2").hasRole("ADMIN") // covered by the earlier "/test1/**"
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );

Correct (most specific first):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/home").hasRole("USER")
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/test2").hasRole("ADMIN")
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/**").hasRole("USER")
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );
target:
Meldet Request-Matcher in einer authorizeHttpRequests- / authorizeRequests-Kette, die nicht erreichbar sind, weil ein früherer, allgemeinerer Matcher sie bereits abdeckt.

Spring Security wertet Matcher in der Deklarationsreihenfolge aus, und die erste passende Regel gewinnt. Eine spezifische Regel, die nach einer allgemeineren steht, die ebenfalls passt, wird daher stillschweigend ignoriert. Spezifischere Matcher müssen zuerst stehen.

Falsch (die markierten Regeln werden ignoriert):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/home").hasRole("USER")        // durch das frühere "/home" abgedeckt
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/**").hasRole("USER")
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/test2").hasRole("ADMIN") // durch das frühere "/test1/**" abgedeckt
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );

Richtig (spezifischste zuerst):


  http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/home").hasRole("USER")
    .requestMatchers("/", "/home").permitAll()
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/test2").hasRole("ADMIN")
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/test1/**").hasRole("USER")
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
  );

source:
Reports I/O resources that are not safely closed. I/O resources checked by this inspection include java.io.InputStream, java.io.OutputStream, java.io.Reader, java.io.Writer, java.util.zip.ZipFile, java.io.Closeable and java.io.RandomAccessFile.

I/O resources wrapped by other I/O resources are not reported, as the wrapped resource will be closed by the wrapping resource.

By default, the inspection assumes that the resources can be closed by any method with 'close' or 'cleanup' in its name.

Example:


  void save() throws IOException {
    FileWriter writer = new FileWriter("filename.txt"); //warning
    writer.write("sample");
  }

Use the following options to configure the inspection:

  • List I/O resource classes that do not need to be closed and should be ignored by this inspection.
  • Whether an I/O resource is allowed to be opened inside a tryblock. This style is less desirable because it is more verbose than opening a resource in front of a try block.
  • Whether the resource can be closed by any method call with the resource passed as argument.
target:
Meldet E/A-Ressourcen, die nicht sicher geschlossen werden. Zu den von dieser Inspection geprüften E/A-Ressourcen gehören java.io.InputStream, java.io.OutputStream, java.io.Reader, java.io.Writer, java.util.zip.ZipFile, java.io.Closeable und java.io.RandomAccessFile.

E/A-Ressourcen, die von anderen E/A-Ressourcen umschlossen werden, werden nicht gemeldet, da die umschlossene Ressource von der umschließenden Ressource geschlossen wird.

Standardmäßig geht die Inspection davon aus, dass die Ressourcen von jeder Methode geschlossen werden können, die 'close' oder 'cleanup' im Namen enthält.

Beispiel:


  void save() throws IOException {
    FileWriter writer = new FileWriter("filename.txt"); //warning
    writer.write("sample");
  }

Verwenden Sie die folgenden Optionen, um die Inspection zu konfigurieren:

  • Auflistung von E/A-Ressourcenklassen, die nicht geschlossen werden müssen und von dieser Inspection ignoriert werden sollen.
  • Ob eine E/A-Ressource innerhalb eines try-Blocks geöffnet werden darf. Dieser Stil ist weniger wünschenswert, da er ausführlicher ist als das Öffnen einer Ressource vor einem try-Block.
  • Ob die Ressource durch einen beliebigen Methodenaufruf geschlossen werden kann, bei dem die Ressource als Argument übergeben wird.

Reports calls and accesses of CoroutineScope extensions or members inside suspend functions with CoroutineScope receiver.

When a function is suspend and has CoroutineScope receiver, it has ambiguous access to CoroutineContext via kotlin.coroutines.coroutineContext and via CoroutineScope.coroutineContext, and two these contexts are different in general.

To improve this situation, one can wrap suspicious call inside coroutineScope { ... } or get rid of CoroutineScope function receiver.
target:
Meldet Aufrufe und Zugriffe von CoroutineScope-Erweiterungen oder -Membern innerhalb von Suspend-Funktionen mit CoroutineScope-Receiver.

Wenn eine Funktion suspend ist und einen CoroutineScope-Receiver hat, hat sie mehrdeutigen Zugriff auf CoroutineContext über kotlin.coroutines.coroutineContext und über CoroutineScope.coroutineContext, und diese beiden Kontexte unterscheiden sich im Allgemeinen.

Um diese Situation zu verbessern, kann man den verdächtigen Aufruf in coroutineScope { ... } einbetten oder den CoroutineScope-Funktionsreceiver entfernen.

Reports <bean> names that don't follow the bean naming conventions.

The convention is to use the standard Java convention for instance field names when naming beans. That is, bean names start with a lowercase letter and are camel-cased from there. Examples of such names include accountManager, accountService, userDao, loginController, and so on. Naming beans consistently makes your configuration easier to read and understand. Also, if you are using Spring AOP, it helps a lot when applying an advice to a set of beans related by name.

Das heißt, Bean-Namen beginnen mit einem Kleinbuchstaben und sind von dort an in CamelCase geschrieben. Beispiele für solche Namen sind accountManager, accountService, userDao, loginController usw. Eine konsistente Benennung von Beans macht Ihre Konfiguration leichter lesbar und verständlich.         GET("/test/{var}") { ServerResponse.ok().body("${it.pathVariable("bar")}") }
    }
}

After the fix is applied:


@Configuration
class RouterConfiguration {
    @Bean
    fun myRouter() = router {
        GET("/test/{var}") { ServerResponse.ok().body("${it.pathVariable("var")}") }
    }
}

        GET("/test/{var}") { ServerResponse.ok().body("${it.pathVariable("bar")}") }
    }

source:
Reports an explicit context argument that can be converted to an implicit one by wrapping the call in a context(...) { } block.

Context parameters are implicit: their values are resolved from in-scope context parameters and implicit receivers. Wrapping the call in a context block adds the value to the context, making it available for implicit resolution.

Example:


  interface Logger { fun log(message: String) }

  context(logger: Logger)
  fun logWithTime(message: String) {
      logger.log("${LocalDateTime.now()}: $message")
  }

  fun saveUser(user: User, logger: Logger) {
      logWithTime("saving user ${user.id}", logger = logger)
  }

The quick-fix wraps the call in a context block:


  fun saveUser(user: User, logger: Logger) {
      context(logger) {
          logWithTime("saving user ${user.id}")
      }
  }
target:
Meldet ein explizites Kontextargument, das durch Einschließen des Aufrufs in einen context(...) { }-Block in ein implizites umgewandelt werden kann.

Kontextparameter sind implizit: Ihre Werte werden aus den im Gültigkeitsbereich vorhandenen Kontextparametern und impliziten Empfängern aufgelöst. Durch Einschließen des Aufrufs in einen context-Block wird der Wert dem Kontext hinzugefügt und für die implizite Auflösung verfügbar gemacht.

Beispiel:


  interface Logger { fun log(message: String) }

  context(logger: Logger)
  fun logWithTime(message: String) {
      logger.log("${LocalDateTime.now()}: $message")
  }

  fun saveUser(user: User, logger: Logger) {
      logWithTime("saving user ${user.id}", logger = logger)
  }

Der Quick-Fix schließt den Aufruf in einen context-Block ein:


  fun saveUser(user: User, logger: Logger) {
      context(logger) {
          logWithTime("saving user ${user.id}")
      }
  }

Reports numeric values returned from methods that don't conform to the declared method return range. You can declare method return range using a number of annotations:
  • org.jetbrains.annotations.Range from JetBrains annotations package (specify 'from' and 'to')
  • org.checkerframework.common.value.qual.IntRange from Checker Framework annotations package (specify 'from' and 'to')
  • org.checkerframework.checker.index.qual.GTENegativeOne from Checker Framework annotations package (range is '>= -1')
  • org.checkerframework.checker.index.qual.NonNegative from Checker Framework annotations package (range is '>= 0')
  • org.checkerframework.checker.index.qual.Positive from Checker Framework annotations package (range is '> 0')
  • javax.annotation.Nonnegative from JSR 305 annotations package (range is '>= 0')
  • javax.validation.constraints.Min (specify minimum value)
  • javax.validation.constraints.Max (specify maximum value)

Example:


  @Range(from = 0, to = Integer.MAX_VALUE) int getValue() {
    // Warning: -1 is outside of declared range
    return -1;
  }

New in 2021.2
target:

Reports calls to wait() made on a java.util.concurrent.locks.Condition object. This is probably a programming error, and some variant of the await() method was intended instead.

Example:


  void acquire(Condition released) throws InterruptedException {
    while (acquired) {
      released.wait();
    }
  }

Good code would look like this:


  void acquire(Condition released) throws InterruptedException {
    while (acquired) {
      released.await();
    }
  }
target:

  void acquire(Condition released) throws InterruptedException {
    while (acquired) {
      released.wait();
    }
  }

Guter Code würde so aussehen:


  void acquire(Condition released) throws InterruptedException {
    while (acquired) {
      released.await();
    }
  }

Reports Javadoc comments that contain only an {@inheritDoc} tag. Since Javadoc copies the super class' comment if no comment is present, a comment containing only {@inheritDoc} adds nothing.

Also, it reports the {@inheritDoc} usages in invalid locations, for example, in fields.

Suggests removing the unnecessary Javadoc comment.

Example:


  class Example implements Comparable<Example> {
    /**
     * {@inheritDoc}
     */
    @Override
    public int compareTo(Example o) {
      return 0;
    }
  }

After the quick-fix is applied:


  class Example implements Comparable<Example> {
    @Override
    public int compareTo(Example o) {
      return 0;
    }
  }

Reports equals() calls on enum constants.

Such calls can be replaced by an identity comparison (==) because two enum constants are equal only when they have the same identity.

A quick-fix is available to change the call to a comparison.

Example:


  boolean foo(MyEnum value) {
    return value.equals(MyEnum.FOO);
  }

After the quick-fix is applied:


  boolean foo(MyEnum value) {
    return value == MyEnum.FOO;
  }

Ein Quick-Fix ist verfügbar, um den Aufruf in einen Vergleich umzuwandeln.

Beispiel:


  boolean foo(MyEnum value) {
    return value.equals(MyEnum.FOO);
  }

Nachdem der Quick-Fix angewendet wurde:

    return value == MyEnum.FOO;
  }

Suggests replacing initialization of fields using assignment with initialization in the field declaration.

Only reports if the field assignment is located in an instance or static initializer, and joining it with the field declaration is likely to be safe. In other cases, like assignment inside a constructor, the quick-fix is provided without highlighting, as the fix may change the semantics.

Example:


  class MyClass {
    static final int intConstant;
    
    static {
      intConstant = 10;
    }
  }
The quick fix moves the assigned value to the field initializer removing the class initializer if possible: 

  class MyClass {
    static final int intConstant = 10;
  }
Since 2017.2
target:

In anderen Fällen, wie einer Zuweisung innerhalb eines Konstruktors, wird der Quick-Fix ohne Hervorhebung angeboten, da der Fix die Semantik ändern kann.

Beispiel:


  class MyClass {
    static final int intConstant;
    
    static {
      intConstant = 10;
    }
  }
Der Quick-Fix verschiebt den zugewiesenen Wert in den Feldinitialisierer und entfernt den Klasseninitialisierer, falls möglich:

    static final int intConstant = 10;
  }

Reports issues with AtomicLongFieldUpdater, AtomicIntegerFieldUpdater, or AtomicReferenceFieldUpdater fields (the java.util.concurrent.atomic package).

The reported issues are identical to the runtime problems that can happen with atomic field updaters: specified field not found, specified field not accessible, specified field has a wrong type, and so on.

Examples:

  • 
  class A {
    private static volatile int value = 0;
    private static final AtomicIntegerFieldUpdater updater =
    AtomicIntegerFieldUpdater.newUpdater((A.class), "value"); // warning: Field 'value' has 'static' modifier
  }
  
  • 
  class B {
    private static final AtomicIntegerFieldUpdater updater =
      AtomicIntegerFieldUpdater.newUpdater(B.class, "value"); // warning: No field named 'value' found in class 'B'
  }
target:

Beispiele:

    private static volatile int value = 0;
    private static final AtomicIntegerFieldUpdater updater =

  }

Reports Persistence ORM XML descriptors that cannot be resolved within the configured datasource and suggests refreshing the datasource or assigning a different one.

Example database table:


  CREATE TABLE DATA_TABLE (
    ID INTEGER,
    DATA VARCHAR(100)
  );

Example JSP file:


  <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
  <entity-mappings xmlns="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/persistence/orm" version="1.0">
    <entity name="JavaEntity" class="JavaEntity">
        <table name="UNKNOWN_TABLE"/> // Error: unresolved table
        <attributes>
          <id name="id">
            <column name="ID" nullable="false"/>
          </id>
          <basic name="UNKNOWN_COLUMN"> // Error: unresolved column
            <column name="UNKNOWN_COLUMN" length="12"/>
          </basic>
        </attributes>
    </entity>
  </entity-mappings>

NOTE: Datasource can be configured via `Assign datasource` action
target:

  CREATE TABLE DATA_TABLE (
    ID INTEGER,
    DATA VARCHAR(100)
  );

Beispiel für eine JSP-Datei:


  <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
  <entity-mappings xmlns="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/persistence/orm" version="1.0">
    <entity name="JavaEntity" class="JavaEntity">
        <table name="UNKNOWN_TABLE"/> // Fehler: nicht aufgelöste Tabelle
        <attributes>
          <id name="id">
            <column name="ID" nullable="false"/>
          </id>
          <basic name="UNKNOWN_COLUMN"> // Fehler: nicht aufgelöste Spalte
            <column name="UNKNOWN_COLUMN" length="12"/>

Reports code that uses of == or != to compare strings.

These operators determine referential equality instead of comparing content. In most cases, strings should be compared using equals(), which does a character-by-character comparison when the strings are different objects.

Example:


  void foo(String s, String t) {
    final boolean b = t == s;
  }

If t is known to be non-null, then it's safe to apply the "unsafe" quick-fix and get the result similar to the following:


  void foo(String s, String t) {
    final boolean b = t.equals(s);
  }
target:
Meldet Code, der == oder != zum Vergleich von Strings verwendet.

Diese Operatoren prüfen Referenzgleichheit statt Inhalte zu vergleichen. In den meisten Fällen sollten Strings mit equals() verglichen werden, das einen zeichenweisen Vergleich durchführt, wenn die Strings unterschiedliche Objekte sind.

Beispiel:


  void foo(String s, String t) {
    final boolean b = t == s;
  }

Wenn bekannt ist, dass t nicht null ist, kann der "unsichere" Schnellfix angewendet werden, um ein Ergebnis ähnlich dem folgenden zu erhalten:


  void foo(String s, String t) {
    final boolean b = t.equals(s);
  }

source: Diff isn't shown because the content before the turn wasn't saved.

(Gradle 4.9+) Detects usage of API that interacts with tasks eagerly.

Eager interaction with tasks implies some inconveniences:

  • The user should manually set up all dependencies between tasks;
  • In the configuration phase, all the tasks accessed via the eager API become configured, even if they are not executed afterwards. It results in performance degradation.

Eventually, the eager API will be deprecated in favor of the lazy one.

For a migration guide, see the Gradle documentation.

Example:

task foo { // reports 'task', suggests replacing it with 'task.register'
  // ...
}
target:
(Gradle 4.9+) Erkennt die Verwendung von API, die Tasks eager verarbeitet.

Eager-Interaktion mit Tasks bringt einige Nachteile mit sich:

  • Der Benutzer muss alle Abhängigkeiten zwischen Tasks manuell einrichten;
  • In der Konfigurationsphase werden alle über die Eager-API zugegriffenen Tasks konfiguriert, auch wenn sie danach nicht ausgeführt werden. Das führt zu Leistungseinbußen.

Letztlich wird die Eager-API zugunsten der Lazy-API veraltet.

Reports errors in date and time literals. This inspection is available in MySQL, Oracle, Db2, and H2.

Example (MySQL):

SELECT TIME '10 -12:13:14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME ' 12 : 13 : 14 ' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12 13 14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12-13-14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12.13.14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:13:' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:13' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:' FROM dual;

In this example, dates ignore the MySQL standard for date and time literals. Therefore, they will be highlighted. For more information about date and time literals in MySQL, see Date and Time Literals at dev.mysql.com.

The following date and type literals are valid for MySQL.

SELECT TIME '12:13:14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:13:14.555' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:13:14.' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '-12:13:14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '10 12:13:14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '-10 12:13:14' FROM dual;

SELECT TIME '10 -12:13:14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME ' 12 : 13 : 14 ' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12 13 14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12-13-14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12.13.14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:13:' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:13' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:' FROM dual;

In diesem Beispiel ignorieren die Datumsangaben den MySQL-Standard für Datums- und Zeitliterale. Daher werden sie hervorgehoben. Weitere Informationen zu Datums- und Zeitliteralen in MySQL finden Sie unter Date and Time Literals bei dev.mysql.com.

Die folgenden Datums- und Typliterale sind für MySQL gültig.

SELECT TIME '12:13:14' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:13:14.555' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '12:13:14.' FROM dual;
SELECT TIME '-12:13:14' FROM dual;

source:
Applies to new Spring Application that are created by invoking New | Spring Component | Application in the Project tool window.
This built-in template is editable. Along with Java expressions and comments, you can also use the predefined variables (listed below) that will then be expanded like macros into corresponding values.

It is also possible to specify custom variables. Custom variables use the following format: ${VARIABLE_NAME}, where VARIABLE_NAME is a name for your variable (for example, ${MY_CUSTOM_FUNCTION_NAME}). Before the IDE creates a new file with custom variables, you see a dialog where you can define values for custom variables in the template.

By using the #parse directive, you can include templates from the Includes tab. To include a template, specify the full name of the template as a parameter in quotation marks (for example, #parse("File Header.java").
Predefined variables take the following values:
${PACKAGE_NAME}   Name of the package in which a new class is created
${NAME}   Name of the new class specified by you in the Create New Class dialog
${USER}   System login name of the current user
${DATE}   Current system date
${TIME}   Current system time
${YEAR}   Current year
${MONTH}   Current month
${MONTH_NAME_SHORT}   First 3 letters of the current month name (Jan, Feb, and so on)
${MONTH_NAME_FULL}   Full name of the current month (January, February, and so on)
${DAY}   Current day of the month
${HOUR}   Current hour
${MINUTE}   Current minute
${PROJECT_NAME}   Name of the current project
target:
Gilt für neue Spring-Anwendungen, die durch Aufrufen von New | Spring Component | Application im Werkzeugfenster Project erstellt werden.
Diese eingebaute Vorlage ist bearbeitbar. Neben Java-Ausdrücken und Kommentaren können Sie auch die vordefinierten Variablen verwenden (unten aufgeführt), die dann wie Makros zu entsprechenden Werten expandiert werden.

Es ist auch möglich, benutzerdefinierte Variablen anzugeben. Benutzerdefinierte Variablen verwenden das folgende Format: ${VARIABLE_NAME}, wobei VARIABLE_NAME ein Name für Ihre Variable ist (zum Beispiel ${MY_CUSTOM_FUNCTION_NAME}). Bevor die IDE eine neue Datei mit benutzerdefinierten Variablen erstellt, sehen Sie einen Dialog, in dem Sie Werte für benutzerdefinierte Variablen in der Vorlage definieren können.

Mit der Direktive #parse können Sie Vorlagen aus dem Tab Includes einbinden. Um eine Vorlage einzubinden, geben Sie den vollständigen Namen der Vorlage als Parameter in Anführungszeichen an (zum Beispiel #parse("File Header.java").
Vordefinierte Variablen nehmen die folgenden Werte an:
${PACKAGE_NAME}   Name des Pakets, in dem eine neue Klasse erstellt wird
${NAME}   Name der neuen Klasse, den Sie im Dialog Create New Class angegeben haben
${USER}   System-Anmeldename des aktuellen Benutzers
${DATE}   Aktuelles Systemdatum
${TIME}   Aktuelle Systemzeit
${YEAR}   Aktuelles Jahr
${MONTH}   Aktueller Monat
${MONTH_NAME_SHORT}   Die ersten 3 Buchstaben des aktuellen Monatsnamens (Jan, Feb usw.)

${DAY}   Aktueller Tag des Monats

${MINUTE}   Aktuelle Minute

Defines template which used to generate JavaDoc for the overriding methods, e.g. when Add Javadoc intention action is applied.

${PARAMS}   List of the parameter names
${TYPE_PARAMS}   List of the type parameter names
${THROWS}   List of the thrown exceptions
${RETURN_TYPE}   Type returned by the method
${PARAMS_INHERITED}   List of the parameters with descriptions of the super method
${ELEMENT_NAME}   Name of the class member which is owner for the generated JavaDoc
${CONTAINING_CLASS}   Name of the parent class
${SUPER_METHOD}   Fully qualified name of the super method
${PACKAGE_NAME}   Name of the package in which a new enum is created
${NAME}   Name of the new enum specified by you in the Create New Class dialog
${USER}   System login name of the current user
${DATE}   Current system date
${TIME}   Current system time
${YEAR}   Current year
${MONTH}   Current month

source:
Logpoints is a debugger feature that enables printing expressions (kotlin.io.println) to the standard output without changing the source code. It has a few advantages over common println in source code:
  • Logpoints can be added, modified, and removed during execution, no need to hot-reload;
  • As a consequence, they can be used in library code, which cannot be manually changed;
  • Logpoints may not even compile, it wouldn't affect the program execution;
  • There is no risk of leaking printing calls into production, as logpoints are not part of the source code.
The inspection only works if there's an executable line after the println call, and this line is not a loop statement. This restriction is made because breakpoints work differently at these places, and the replacement is not equivalent.
NOTE: Logpoints only work in Debug mode. In Run, Run with Coverage, Profile modes, logpoint expressions won't appear in the output.
target:
Logpoints sind eine Debugger-Funktion, mit der Ausdrücke (kotlin.io.println) auf die Standardausgabe gedruckt werden können ohne den Quellcode zu ändern. Sie bieten einige Vorteile gegenüber gewöhnlichem println im Quellcode:
  • Logpoints können während der Ausführung hinzugefügt, geändert und entfernt werden – kein Hot-Reload nötig;
  • Dadurch können sie in Bibliothekscode verwendet werden, der nicht manuell geändert werden kann;
  • Logpoints müssen nicht einmal kompilieren, das würde die Programmausführung nicht beeinträchtigen;
  • Es besteht kein Risiko, dass Druckaufrufe in die Produktion gelangen, da Logpoints nicht Teil des Quellcodes sind.
Die Inspektion funktioniert nur, wenn nach dem println-Aufruf eine ausführbare Zeile folgt und diese Zeile keine Schleifenanweisung ist. Diese Einschränkung besteht, weil Breakpoints an diesen Stellen anders funktionieren und die Ersetzung nicht äquivalent ist.
HINWEIS: Logpoints funktionieren nur im Debug-Modus. In den Modi Run, Run with Coverage und Profile erscheinen Logpoint-Ausdrücke nicht in der Ausgabe.

source:
Reports code constructs that always violate nullability contracts, may throw exceptions, or are just redundant, based on data flow analysis.

Examples:

if (array.length < index) {
  System.out.println(array[index]);
} // Array index is always out of bounds

if (str == null) System.out.println("str is null");
System.out.println(str.trim());
// the last statement may throw an NPE

@NotNull
Integer square(@Nullable Integer input) {
    // the method contract is violated
    return input == null ? null : input * input;
}

The inspection behavior may be controlled by a number of annotations, such as nullability annotations, @Contract annotation, @Range annotation and so on.

Configure the inspection:

  • Use the Suggest @Nullable annotation for methods/fields/parameters where nullable values are used option to warn when a nullable value is passed as an argument to a method with a non-annotated parameter, stored into non-annotated field, or returned from a non-annotated method. In this case, the inspection will suggest propagating the @Nullable annotation. You can also configure nullability annotations using the Configure Annotations button.
  • Use the Treat non-annotated members and parameters as @Nullable option to assume that non-annotated members can be null, so they must not be used in non-null context.
  • Use the Report not-null required parameter with null-literal argument usages option to report method parameters that cannot be null (e.g. immediately dereferenced in the method body), but there are call sites where a null literal is passed.
  • Use the Report nullable methods that always return a non-null value option to report methods that are annotated as @Nullable, but always return non-null value. In this case, it's suggested that you change the annotation to @NotNull.
  • Use the Ignore assert statements option to control how the inspection treats assert statements. By default, the option is disabled, which means that the assertions are assumed to be executed (-ea mode). If the option is enabled, the assertions will be completely ignored (-da mode).
  • Use the Reports patterns that may throw MatchException option to report patterns that may throw MatchException at runtime due to null values in deconstruction patterns.
  • Use the Report problems that happen only on some code paths option to control whether to report problems that may happen only on some code path. If this option is disabled, warnings like exception is possible will not be reported. The inspection will report only warnings like exception will definitely occur. This mode may greatly reduce the number of false-positives, especially if the code is not consistently annotated with nullability and contract annotations. That is why it can be useful for finding the most important problems in legacy code bases.
  • Use the Report nullable values for type variables with unspecified nullness bound (returns and fields) option to report returning a null or nullable value from a method, or storing it into a field, whose type is a type variable with an unspecified nullness bound. Such a type variable may be instantiated with a non-null type at the use site, so producing a null value for it is potentially unsound. Type variables with an explicit @Nullable bound are always reported, regardless of this option.

Before IntelliJ IDEA 2022.3, this inspection was part of the "Constant Conditions & Exceptions" inspection. Now, it is split into two inspections: "Constant Values" and "Nullability and data flow problems".

Reports empty methods that can be removed.

Methods are considered empty if they are empty themselves and if they are overridden or implemented by empty methods only. Note that methods containing only comments and the super() call with own parameters are also considered empty.

The inspection ignores methods with special annotations, for example, the javax.ejb.Init and javax.ejb.Remove EJB annotations .

The quick-fix safely removes unnecessary methods.

Configure the inspection:

  • Use the Comments and javadoc count as content option to select whether methods with comments should be treated as non-empty.
  • Use the Additional special annotations option to configure additional annotations that should be ignored by this inspection.
target:

Die Inspektion ignoriert Methoden mit speziellen Annotationen, zum Beispiel den EJB-Annotationen javax.ejb.Init und javax.ejb.Remove.

Der Quick-Fix entfernt unnötige Methoden sicher.

Konfigurieren Sie die Inspektion:

  • Verwenden Sie die Option Kommentare und Javadoc als Inhalt zählen, um auszuwählen, ob Methoden mit Kommentaren als nicht leer behandelt werden sollen.

Reports private methods which are only called from an inner class of the class containing the method. Such methods can be safely moved into that inner class.

Example:


public class Outer {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    new Inner().run(args[0]);
  }

  static class Inner {
    void run(String arg) {
      // Method isEmpty() is used from Inner class only
      // consider moving it to the Inner class
      if (!isEmpty(arg)) {
        System.out.println("Argument is supplied");
      }
    }
  }

  private static boolean isEmpty(String s) {
    return s != null && s.trim().isEmpty();
  }
}

Use the first checkbox below to ignore private methods which are called from an anonymous or local class.

Use the third checkbox to only report static methods.

Reports attempts to create NOT NULL columns without DEFAULT values.

Example (Microsoft SQL Server):

CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b  INT)

ALTER TABLE foo ADD c INT NOT NULL;

By default, a column holds NULL values. In the example, we use the NOT NULL constraint that enforces a column not to accept NULL values. If we prohibit to use NULL values, we must set the DEFAULT value that SQL can use when we create a new record. 

ALTER TABLE foo ADD c INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 42;

You can quickly add the DEFAULT value by using the Add DEFAULT value quick-fix.

Reports 'fall-through' in a switch statement.

Fall-through occurs when a series of executable statements after a case label is not guaranteed to transfer control before the next case label. For example, this can happen if the branch is missing a break statement. In that case, control falls through to the statements after that switch label, even though the switch expression is not equal to the value of the fallen-through label. While occasionally intended, this construction is confusing and is often the result of a typo.

This inspection ignores any fall-through commented with a text matching the regex pattern (?i)falls?\s*thro?u.

There is a fix that adds a break to the branch that can fall through to the next branch.

Example:


    switch(x) {
      case (4):
          if (condition) {
              System.out.println("3");
              // no break here
          } else {
              break;
          }
      case (6):
          System.out.println("4");
    }

After the quick-fix is applied:


    switch(x) {
        case (4):
            if (condition) {
                System.out.println("3");
            } else {
                break;
            }
            break;
        case (6):
            System.out.println("4");
    }
target:
Meldet 'Fall-Through' in einer switch-Anweisung.

Fall-Through tritt auf, wenn eine Reihe von ausführbaren Anweisungen nach einem case-Label nicht garantiert die Kontrolle vor dem nächsten case-Label übergibt. Zum Beispiel kann dies passieren, wenn im Zweig eine break-Anweisung fehlt. In diesem Fall fällt die Kontrolle in die Anweisungen nach diesem switch-Label, obwohl der switch-Ausdruck nicht gleich dem Wert des durchgefallenen Labels ist. Obwohl gelegentlich beabsichtigt, ist diese Konstruktion verwirrend und oft das Ergebnis eines Tippfehlers.

Diese Inspektion ignoriert jeden Fall-Through, der mit einem Text kommentiert ist, der dem regulären Ausdruck (?i)falls?\s*thro?u entspricht.

Es gibt einen Fix, der ein break zum Zweig hinzufügt, der zum nächsten Zweig durchfallen kann.

Beispiel:


    switch(x) {
      case (4):
          if (condition) {
              System.out.println("3");
              // no break here
          } else {
              break;
          }
      case (6):
          System.out.println("4");
    }

Nach Anwendung des Schnellfixes:


    switch(x) {
        case (4):
            if (condition) {
                System.out.println("3");
            } else {
                break;
            }
            break;
        case (6):
            System.out.println("4");
    }

Reports Double Brace Initialization.

Compared to regular initialization, double brace initialization provides worse performance since it requires loading an additional class.

It may also cause failure of equals() comparisons if the equals() method doesn't accept subclasses as parameters.

Double brace initialization may cause memory leaks when used in a non-static context. This is because it defines an anonymous class that will reference the surrounding object, when compiled with javac from before Java 18.

In addition, before Java 9, double brace initialization couldn't be combined with the diamond operator since it was incompatible with anonymous classes.

Example:


  List<Integer> list = new ArrayList<>() {{
    add(1);
    add(2);
  }};

After the quick-fix is applied:


  List<Integer> list = new ArrayList<>();
  list.add(1);
  list.add(2);
target:
Meldet Double Brace Initialization.

Im Vergleich zur regulären Initialisierung bietet die Double-Brace-Initialisierung eine schlechtere Performance, da eine zusätzliche Klasse geladen werden muss.

Sie kann auch zum Fehlschlagen von equals()-Vergleichen führen, wenn die equals()-Methode keine Unterklassen als Parameter akzeptiert.

Double-Brace-Initialisierung kann Speicherlecks verursachen, wenn sie in einem nicht-statischen Kontext verwendet wird. Dies liegt daran, dass sie eine anonyme Klasse definiert, die auf das umgebende Objekt verweist, wenn sie mit javac vor Java 18 kompiliert wird.

Außerdem konnte vor Java 9 die Double-Brace-Initialisierung nicht mit dem Diamond-Operator kombiniert werden, da dieser inkompatibel mit anonymen Klassen war.

Reports getClass() methods that are called on a java.lang.Class instance.

This is usually a mistake as the result is always equivalent to Class.class. If it's a mistake, then it's better to remove the getClass() call and use the qualifier directly. If the behavior is intended, then it's better to write Class.class explicitly to avoid confusion.

Example:


  void test(Class<?> clazz) {
    String name = clazz.getClass().getName();
  }

After one of the possible quick-fixes is applied:


  void test(Class<?> clazz) {
    String name = clazz.getName();
  }

New in 2018.2
target:

  void test(Class<?> clazz) {

source:
Reports incorrect usages of transition table variables in triggers.

Example (HSQLDB):

CREATE TABLE foo(a INT);

CREATE TRIGGER trg
 AFTER DELETE ON foo
BEGIN
   SELECT * FROM NEW;
END;

CREATE TRIGGER trig AFTER INSERT ON foo
   REFERENCING OLD ROW AS newrow
   FOR EACH ROW WHEN (a > 1)
   INSERT INTO foo VALUES (1)

In HSQLDB, DELETE triggers may be used only with the OLD state while INSERT triggers may have only the NEW state. So, in the previous example, NEW in SELECT * FROM NEW; will be highlighted as well as OLD in REFERENCING OLD ROW AS newrow.
target:
Meldet inkorrekte Verwendungen von Transition-Table-Variablen in Triggern.

Beispiel (HSQLDB):

CREATE TABLE foo(a INT);

CREATE TRIGGER trg
 AFTER DELETE ON foo
BEGIN
   SELECT * FROM NEW;
END;

CREATE TRIGGER trig AFTER INSERT ON foo
   REFERENCING OLD ROW AS newrow
   FOR EACH ROW WHEN (a > 1)
   INSERT INTO foo VALUES (1)

In HSQLDB dürfen DELETE-Trigger nur mit dem OLD-Zustand verwendet werden, während INSERT-Trigger nur den NEW-Zustand haben dürfen. Im vorherigen Beispiel wird also NEW in SELECT * FROM NEW; ebenso hervorgehoben wie OLD in REFERENCING OLD ROW AS newrow.

source:
Reports instance methods with the same name and the same number of parameters as a method in a superclass, but where at least one of the parameters is of a different incompatible type.

In this case, the method in a subclass will be overloading the method from the superclass instead of overriding it. If it is unintended, it may result in latent bugs.

Example:


  public class Foo {
    void foo(int x) {}
  }

  public class Bar extends Foo {
    void foo(Number x) {} // Method 'foo()' overloads a compatible method of a superclass,
                          // when overriding might have been intended
  }

Use the option to choose whether the inspection should also report cases where parameter types are not compatible.
target:
Meldet Instanzmethoden mit demselben Namen und derselben Anzahl von Parametern wie eine Methode in einer Superklasse, aber bei denen mindestens einer der Parameter einen anderen inkompatiblen Typ hat.

In diesem Fall überlädt die Methode in der Subklasse die Methode aus der Superklasse, anstatt sie zu überschreiben. Wenn dies nicht beabsichtigt ist, kann es zu versteckten Fehlern führen.

Beispiel:


  public class Foo {
    void foo(int x) {}
  }

  public class Bar extends Foo {
    void foo(Number x) {} // Methode 'foo()' überlädt eine kompatible Methode einer Superklasse,
                          // obwohl möglicherweise ein Überschreiben beabsichtigt war
  }

Verwenden Sie die Option, um festzulegen, ob die Inspektion auch Fälle melden soll, in denen Parametertypen nicht kompatibel sind.

source: Generate OpenAPI documentation for current module

Detects possibly misplaced calls to Gradle methods.

Gradle buildscripts comprise a lot of nested closures, making the code structure similar to a markup language. Due to the behavior of DSL languages, the methods that you can write in the outer closures are also available in the inner ones. Such methods may have no meaning when written outside their scope.
Sometimes it may be hard to detect this situation. This inspection aims to detect such methods.

Example:


repositories {
  // the delegate of 'repositories' has method 'exclusiveContent', which can be written here
  maven {
    // the delegate of 'maven' has method 'content', which can be written here
    // but 'exclusiveContent' is also available
    exclusiveContent {} // reports 'exclusiveContent'
  }
}
target:
Erkennt möglicherweise falsch platzierte Aufrufe von Gradle-Methoden.

Gradle-Buildskripte bestehen aus vielen verschachtelten Closures, wodurch die Codestruktur einer Markup-Sprache ähnelt. Aufgrund des Verhaltens von DSL-Sprachen sind die Methoden, die man in den äußeren Closures schreiben kann, auch in den inneren verfügbar. Solche Methoden können außerhalb ihres Geltungsbereichs bedeutungslos sein.
Manchmal kann es schwierig sein, diese Situation zu erkennen. Diese Inspection zielt darauf ab, solche Methoden zu erkennen.

Beispiel:


repositories {
  // der Delegate von 'repositories' hat die Methode 'exclusiveContent', die hier geschrieben werden kann
  maven {
    // der Delegate von 'maven' hat die Methode 'content', die hier geschrieben werden kann
    // aber 'exclusiveContent' ist ebenfalls verfügbar
    exclusiveContent {} // meldet 'exclusiveContent'
  }
}

source:
Reports redundant calls to String constructors and methods like toString() or substring() that can be replaced with a simpler expression.

For example, calls to these methods can be safely removed in code like "string".substring(0), "string".toString(), or new StringBuilder().toString().substring(1,3).

Example:


  System.out.println(new String("message"));

After the quick-fix is applied:


  System.out.println("message");

Note that the quick-fix removes the redundant constructor call, and this may affect String referential equality. If you need to preserve it, even though it is considered bad practice, suppress the warning or use the inspection setting to ignore redundant String constructor calls.

Use the Do not report String constructor calls option below to not report code like the example above. This will avoid changing the outcome of String comparisons with == or != after applying the quick-fix in code that uses new String() calls to guarantee a different object identity.

Use the Do not report single argument substring() calls option below to not report code like the following. 


  stringBuilder.append(string.substring(5));

which can be replaced with the following. 


  stringBuilder.append(string, 5, string.length());

New in 2018.1
target:
Meldet redundante Aufrufe von String-Konstruktoren und -Methoden wie toString() oder substring(), die durch einen einfacheren Ausdruck ersetzt werden können.

Beispielsweise können Aufrufe dieser Methoden in Code wie "string".substring(0), "string".toString() oder new StringBuilder().toString().substring(1,3) sicher entfernt werden.

Beispiel:


  System.out.println(new String("message"));

Nach Anwenden des Quick-Fix:


  System.out.println("message");

Beachten Sie, dass der Quick-Fix den redundanten Konstruktoraufruf entfernt und dies die Referenzgleichheit von String beeinflussen kann. Wenn Sie diese erhalten möchten, auch wenn dies als schlechte Praxis gilt, unterdrücken Sie die Warnung oder verwenden Sie die Inspektionseinstellung, um redundante String-Konstruktoraufrufe zu ignorieren.

Verwenden Sie unten die Option String-Konstruktoraufrufe nicht melden, um Code wie im obigen Beispiel nicht zu melden. Dies vermeidet, dass sich das Ergebnis von String-Vergleichen mit == oder != nach Anwenden des Quick-Fix in Code ändert, der new String()-Aufrufe verwendet, um eine unterschiedliche Objektidentität zu garantieren.

Applies to new Java annotations that are created by invoking New | Java Class | Annotation in the Project tool window.

This built-in template is editable. Along with Java expressions and comments, you can also use the predefined variables (listed below) that will then be expanded like macros into corresponding values.

It is also possible to specify custom variables. Custom variables use the following format: ${VARIABLE_NAME}, where VARIABLE_NAME is a name for your variable (for example, ${MY_CUSTOM_FUNCTION_NAME}). Before the IDE creates a new file with custom variables, you see a dialog where you can define values for custom variables in the template.

By using the #parse directive, you can include templates from the Includes tab. To include a template, specify the full name of the template as a parameter in quotation marks (for example, #parse("File Header.java").
Predefined variables take the following values:
${PACKAGE_NAME}   Name of the package in which a new annotation is created
${NAME}   Name of the new annotation specified by you in the Create New Class dialog
${USER}   System login name of the current user
${DATE}   Current system date
${TIME}   Current system time
${YEAR}   Current year
${MONTH}   Current month
${MONTH_NAME_SHORT}   First 3 letters of the current month name (Mon, Tue, and so on)
${MONTH_NAME_FULL}   Full name of the current month (January, February, and so on)

source:
Reports expressions of byte type returned from a method implementing the InputStream.read() method.

This is suspicious because InputStream.read() should return a value in the range from 0 to 255, while an expression of byte type contains a value from -128 to 127. The quick-fix converts the expression into an unsigned byte by applying the bitmask 0xFF.

Example:


class MyInputStream extends InputStream {
  int pos = 0;
  byte[] data;

  MyInputStream(byte[] input) {
    data = input;
  }

  @Override
  public int read() {
    if (pos == data.length) {
      return -1;
    }
    return data[pos++]; // problem
  }
}

After applying the quick-fix:


class MyInputStream extends InputStream {
  int pos = 0;
  byte[] data;

  MyInputStream(byte[] input) {
    data = input;
  }

  @Override
  public int read() {
    if (pos == data.length) {
      return -1;
    }
    return data[pos++] & 0xFF;
  }
}

New in 2023.2

Beispiel:


class MyInputStream extends InputStream {

}

    data = input;
  }

source:
Reports duplicate conditions in && and || expressions and branches of if statements. While sometimes duplicate conditions are intended, in most cases they are the result of an oversight.

Example:


  boolean result = digit1 != digit2 || digit1 != digit2;

To ignore conditions that may produce side effects, use the Ignore conditions with side effects option. Disabling this option may lead to false-positives, for example, when the same method returns different values on subsequent invocations.

Example:


  native boolean unknownMethod();
  
  ...
  
  if (unknownMethod() || unknownMethod()) {
    System.out.println("Got it");
  }

Due to possible side effects of unknownMethod() (on the example), the warning will only be triggered if the Ignore conditions with side effects option is disabled.
target:
Meldet doppelte Bedingungen in &&- und ||-Ausdrücken sowie in Zweigen von if-Anweisungen. Manchmal sind doppelte Bedingungen beabsichtigt, in den meisten Fällen sind sie jedoch das Ergebnis eines Versehens.

Beispiel:


  boolean result = digit1 != digit2 || digit1 != digit2;

Um Bedingungen zu ignorieren, die Seiteneffekte haben können, verwenden Sie die Option Bedingungen mit Seiteneffekten ignorieren. Das Deaktivieren dieser Option kann zu Fehlalarmen führen, z.B. wenn dieselbe Methode bei aufeinanderfolgenden Aufrufen unterschiedliche Werte zurückgibt.

Beispiel:


  native boolean unknownMethod();
  
  ...
  
  if (unknownMethod() || unknownMethod()) {

source:
Reports while loops, which spin on the value of a non-volatile field, waiting for it to be changed by another thread.

In addition to being potentially extremely CPU intensive when little work is done inside the loop, such loops likely have different semantics than intended. The Java Memory Model allows that loop to never complete even if another thread changes the field's value.

Example:


  class SpinsOnField {
      boolean ready = false;

      void run() {
          // the loop may never complete even after
          // markAsReady call from the other thread
          while (!ready) {
          }
          // do some work
      }

      void markAsReady() {
          ready = true;
      }
  }

Additionally since Java 9, calling Thread.onSpinWait() inside spin loop on a volatile field is recommended, which may significantly improve performance on some hardware.

Use the checkbox below to have this inspection report only empty while loops.
target:
Meldet while-Schleifen, die auf den Wert eines nicht-volatile-Feldes warten und darauf, dass dieser durch einen anderen Thread geändert wird.

Abgesehen davon, dass sie möglicherweise extrem CPU-intensiv sind, wenn wenig Arbeit innerhalb der Schleife verrichtet wird, haben solche Schleifen wahrscheinlich eine andere Semantik als beabsichtigt. Das Java-Speichermodell erlaubt, dass diese Schleife nie beendet wird, selbst wenn ein anderer Thread den Wert des Feldes ändert.

Beispiel:


  class SpinsOnField {
      boolean ready = false;

      void run() {
          // the loop may never complete even after
          // markAsReady call from the other thread
          while (!ready) {
          }
          // do some work
      }

      void markAsReady() {
          ready = true;
      }
  }

Seit Java 9 wird zusätzlich empfohlen, Thread.onSpinWait() innerhalb einer Spin-Schleife auf einem volatile-Feld aufzurufen, was die Leistung auf mancher Hardware erheblich verbessern kann.

Verwenden Sie das folgende Kontrollkästchen, damit diese Inspektion nur leere while-Schleifen meldet.

Reports calls to Condition.await(), for which no call to a corresponding Condition.signal() or Condition.signalAll() can be found.

Calling Condition.await() in a thread without corresponding Condition.signal() may cause the thread to become disabled until it is interrupted or "spurious wakeup" occurs.

Only calls that target fields of the current class are reported by this inspection.

Example:


  class Queue {

    void add(Object elem) {
      // ...
      // isEmpty.signal();
      // ...
    }

    void remove(Object elem) throws InterruptedException {
      // ...
      isEmpty.await(); // 'await()' doesn't contain corresponding 'signal()'/'signalAll()' call
      // ...

  }

source:
Reports recursive equals(==) calls.

In Kotlin, == compares object values by calling equals method under the hood. ===, on the other hand, compares objects by reference.

=== is commonly used in equals method implementation. But === may be mistakenly mixed up with == leading to infinite recursion.

Example:


  class X {
      override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean {
          if (this == other) return true
          return false
      }
  }

After the quick-fix is applied:


  class X {
      override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean {
          if (this === other) return true
          return false
      }
  }
target:
Meldet rekursive equals-Aufrufe (==).

In Kotlin vergleicht == Objektwerte, indem im Hintergrund die equals-Methode aufgerufen wird. === hingegen vergleicht Objekte per Referenz.

=== wird häufig in der Implementierung der equals-Methode verwendet. === kann jedoch versehentlich mit == verwechselt werden, was zu unendlicher Rekursion führt.

Beispiel:


  class X {
      override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean {
          if (this == other) return true
          return false
      }
  }

Nach Anwendung des Quick-Fix:


  class X {
      override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean {
          if (this === other) return true
          return false
      }
  }

Reports usages of Guava pseudo-functional code when Java Stream API is available.

Though Guava Iterable API provides functionality similar to Java Streams API, it's slightly different and may miss some features. Especially, primitive-specialized stream variants like IntStream are more performant than generic variants.

Example:


List<String> transformedIterable = Iterables.transform(someList, someTransformFunction);//warning: Pseudo functional style code

After the quick-fix is applied:

List<String> transformedIterable = someList.stream().map(someTransformFunction).collect(Collectors.toList());

Note: Code semantics can be changed; for example, Guava's Iterable.transform produces a lazy-evaluated iterable, but the replacement is eager-evaluated.

Beispiel:


List<String> transformedIterable = Iterables.transform(someList, someTransformFunction);//Warnung: Pseudo-funktionaler Stilcode

Nach Anwendung des Quick-Fix:

List<String> transformedIterable = someList.stream().map(someTransformFunction).collect(Collectors.toList());

Hinweis: Die Code-Semantik kann sich ändern; z. B. erzeugt Guavas Iterable.transform ein lazy-ausgewertetes Iterable, während die Ersetzung eager-ausgewertet wird.

Applies to new Spring Application that are created by invoking New | Spring Component | Application in the Project tool window.
This built-in template is editable. Along with Kotlin expressions and comments, you can also use the predefined variables (listed below) that will then be expanded like macros into corresponding values.

It is also possible to specify custom variables. Custom variables use the following format: ${VARIABLE_NAME}, where VARIABLE_NAME is a name for your variable (for example, ${MY_CUSTOM_FUNCTION_NAME}). Before the IDE creates a new file with custom variables, you see a dialog where you can define values for custom variables in the template.

By using the #parse directive, you can include templates from the Includes tab. To include a template, specify the full name of the template as a parameter in quotation marks (for example, #parse("File Header.java").
Predefined variables take the following values:
${PACKAGE_NAME}   Name of the package in which a new class is created
${NAME}   Name of the new class specified by you in the Create New Class dialog
${USER}   System login name of the current user
${DATE}   Current system date
${TIME}   Current system time
${YEAR}   Current year
${MONTH}   Current month
${MONTH_NAME_SHORT}   First 3 letters of the current month name (Jan, Feb, and so on)
${MONTH_NAME_FULL}   Full name of the current month (January, February, and so on)
${DAY}   Current day of the month
${HOUR}   Current hour
${MINUTE}   Current minute
${PROJECT_NAME}   Name of the current project
target:
Gilt für neue Spring-Applications, die durch den Aufruf von New | Spring Component | Application im Werkzeugfenster Project erstellt werden.
Diese eingebaute Vorlage ist editierbar. Neben Kotlin-Ausdrücken und Kommentaren können Sie auch die vordefinierten Variablen (unten aufgelistet) verwenden, die dann wie Makros zu entsprechenden Werten expandiert werden.

Es ist außerdem möglich, benutzerdefinierte Variablen anzugeben. Diese verwenden das folgende Format: ${VARIABLE_NAME}, wobei VARIABLE_NAME der Name Ihrer Variable ist (zum Beispiel ${MY_CUSTOM_FUNCTION_NAME}). Bevor die IDE eine neue Datei mit benutzerdefinierten Variablen erstellt, wird ein Dialog angezeigt, in dem Sie Werte für benutzerdefinierte Variablen in der Vorlage definieren können.

Mit der Direktive #parse können Sie Vorlagen aus dem Reiter Includes einbinden. Um eine Vorlage einzubinden, geben Sie den vollständigen Namen der Vorlage als Parameter in Anführungszeichen an (zum Beispiel #parse("File Header.java").
Vordefinierte Variablen nehmen die folgenden Werte an:
${PACKAGE_NAME}   Name des Pakets, in dem eine neue Klasse erstellt wird
${NAME}   Name der neuen Klasse, den Sie im Dialog Create New Class angegeben haben
${USER}   System-Anmeldename des aktuellen Benutzers
